Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
On 2026-10-31 Kenneth tried to connect his own Bambu P1S through JusPrin's printer chat on this Mac. The model told him "no printer in LAN mode is on the network" twice and fell back on invented Bambu menu paths, because the app's tools reported nothing about what the network search had actually seen: once no search had run yet, and once the P1S had announced itself in cloud mode 7 seconds before the refusal. A fix session (branch `claude/festive-lederberg-693438`) made `printer_connection_status` report the search state and a `seen` list with reasons such as `cloud_mode`, made `printer_connect` refuse with the facts ("P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network with LAN Only off"), posts a note to the model when the first printer appears or after 15 seconds, and in a second commit says when another app holds UDP port 2021 so nothing can be heard. Its no-model harness check against the real P1S passed at 07:30 on 2026-11-01. What nobody has checked is the actual problem: whether a live model, given these new tool results, now tells the person the truth. Kenneth's constraints: live-model runs cost money and are approved one batch at a time (this is one chat); the app must report observations, never guesses; Developer Mode guidance is out of scope until tested on the printer; changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files stay small. Actually connecting the printer (turning LAN Only on at the printer) is a later, separate test.

Task:
Run exactly one live-model chat, with a Sonnet model, through JusPrin's printer chat against Kenneth's real Bambu Lab P1S, and report word for word what the model tells the person. The printer is powered on at 192.168.0.198 in cloud mode (LAN Only off), and it stays that way: do not ask Kenneth to change anything on the printer. Kenneth approved this one chat and no other live-model run.

Code under test: branch `claude/festive-lederberg-693438`, two commits (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) on top of `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4`. Check that branch out in your own worktree. Never touch or build in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`: another session owns it and has temporarily put pre-fix code back there.

How to drive it: `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` has a `--printer-live` mode (documented near line 167, implemented from `begin_printer_live()` near line 3832) that opens the real printer panel with a live model, sends scripted words as the page would, prints every exchange as `HARNESS LIVE` lines, and checks outcomes. It takes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment and `JUSPRIN_LIVE_MODEL` for the model; use a Sonnet model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). Add one scenario flag beside it (say `--printer-live-p1s`) that: copies the real Bambu network plug-in from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/plugins` into the run's throwaway data directory (the `--printer-network-check` scenario on that branch does this; follow it), saves a Bambu Lab P1S printer, opens its Connect chat, and plays the person from the 2026-10-31 incident: ask to connect the printer, and when asked, give the address 192.168.0.198. Wait at least 20 seconds after the first `printer_connection_status` call so the app's note about the printer it saw can reach the model, then send one more line like "so what do I do now?". Print the model's words, every tool call with its result, and the note. Check mechanically: `printer_connection_status` was called; no `printer_connect` succeeded; the model's words name the P1s as seen with LAN Only off and do not claim that no printer is on the network or invent a menu path as fact. Commit the scenario on your branch; keep the run's output and your reading of it in an untracked note at the worktree root (never commit it).

Before the run: `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing (Kenneth's JusPrin, pid 85053 earlier, must be quit; two listeners on that port hide the printer from each other), and no `JusPrinShellHarness` from the other session may be running against the printer (`pgrep -fl JusPrinShellHarness`); wait for it to finish rather than run alongside. Get the API key from Kenneth's `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`/jusprin_agent/...` keys) into the environment without ever printing it; if there is no Anthropic key there and only an OpenRouter one, add the few lines that let the scenario write the OpenRouter provider and key into the throwaway config instead, and use OpenRouter's Sonnet model. Build the harness target only, with `-j4`, after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; the memory file `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md` has the configure line that reuses the existing deps. Failed runs leave a key-holding throwaway data directory: delete only yours.

Done means: the scenario is committed on your branch, the chat ran once against the real P1S with Sonnet, and your report quotes the model's every message, lists the tool calls and the note with their timing, and says plainly whether the model told the person the truth about the printer (seen at 192.168.0.198, LAN Only off) and what to do, or still guessed. Do not merge any branch, do not push, and do not run a second live chat for any reason.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_05f541e9-abc1-4ee8-a987-a295f5fa2c65

Add a harness scenario that plays the printer chat on a real P1S with a live model

The fix for the 2026-10-31 refusal has a no-model check, --printer-network-check,
which shows what the tools report. Nothing yet shows what a live model tells the
person once it reads those results.

--printer-live-p1s <address> copies Bambu's real network plug-in into the run's
throwaway data directory, saves a P1S, opens its Connect chat and plays the person
from that incident through the live model: asks to connect it, gives the address
(when asked, or else before the last line), waits at least 20 seconds into the
search and until the app has reported the printer, then asks what to do. It prints
every message, tool call and note with seconds since the chat opened, and checks
that printer_connection_status was called, that no printer_connect succeeded, and
that the model's words after the report name the P1S and LAN Only, do not say no
printer is there, and hold no menu path. The word checks are a screen for reading
the transcript, not a verdict.

Each run costs one live chat, and it needs the printer on this network.
EOF

content.text:
The live model told the person the truth in the one approved chat against the real P1S: it said the printer was found at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off. It also said connecting is optional and that LAN Only is turned on in the printer's network settings. The scenario is committed on `claude/printer-live-p1s` (`a897a3cbbd`, `5f3bd2e59a`), with nothing merged or pushed, and the printer wasn't changed.

The chat ran at 09:01:48–09:02:46. The provider was Anthropic and the model `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the evidence for the model is the run's app config, because the app's log doesn't record the model name.

## Everything said in the chat
Times are seconds after the chat opened. The opening line comes from the page, not from a model request.

**+0s, page's opening:**
> Let's connect Bambu Lab P1S. Is it turned on, in LAN mode, and on the same network as this computer?
> Choices: Yes, it is | How do I check?

**+0s, person:** Connect my printer

**+9s, model:**
> I'm searching your network for the P1S now. This can take about 15 seconds.

**+21s, app note:**
> The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.

**+25s, model:**
> The app didn't find your P1S on the network. LAN mode may be turned off on the printer, or the printer may be on a different network from this computer.
> On the printer's screen, open the network settings and look for "LAN Only" mode. Is it turned on?
> Choices: Yes, it's on | No, it's off | I can't find it

**+31s, app note:**
> The network search found P1s at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, which cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection.

**+34s, model:**
> Your P1S was found at 192.168.0.198, but LAN Only is off on it, so I can't connect it as it is. To connect it here, you would turn LAN Only on, on the printer's network settings screen. You don't have to, because the printer can prepare prints without a connection.
> Do you want to turn on LAN Only and connect it?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

**+37s, person:** It's at 192.168.0.198

**+41s, model:**
> Thanks. I see it at that address, but it's still in cloud mode, with LAN Only off. I can only connect it once LAN Only is on. You'd turn that on in the printer's network settings.
> Do you want to turn it on and try again, or leave it for now?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

**+44s, person:** so what do I do now?

**+46s, model:**
> You have two options:
> 1. **Connect it:** On the printer's screen, open the network settings and turn on LAN Only. Then tell me, and I'll look for it again. You'll type the access code into a form on this computer, not in this chat.
> 2. **Leave it:** The printer can prepare prints without a connection. You can connect it later from Connect… in its menu on Home.
> Which do you want?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

## Tool calls
The only tool called was `printer_connection_status`, four times, and all four succeeded. The model never called `printer_connect`.

| Time | Search state | Printers in `seen` |
|---|---|---|
| +6s | `started` (0 s) | none |
| +8s | `started` (1 s) | none |
| +22s | `listening` (16 s) | none |
| +38s | `listening` (32 s) | `P1s`, 192.168.0.198, `cloud_mode` |

## Mechanical checks
- **Passed:**
  - The status tool was called.
  - No connect succeeded.
  - The words name the P1S and LAN Only.
  - The words don't claim there is no printer.
- **Failed, but a false alarm:** the no-menu-path check matched "Connect… in its menu on Home", which is a real app menu named in the app's own prompt. I narrowed the word list in `5f3bd2e59a`. The new list compiles and passes on this saved transcript, but hasn't run live.
- **Run result:** the run itself ended `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=1` because of that one check.

## Where the chat still falls short
- **Early "didn't find":** at +25s the model said "The app didn't find your P1S" and sent the person to check the printer, 6 seconds before the printer was heard. That was accurate at that moment and hedged, but it doesn't say the search is still running. The app's 15-second note prompted it.
- **Misleading sentence from the app:** "the printer can prepare prints without a connection" comes from the app's own wording (`kPersonsChoice` in `PrinterConversation.cpp`). It's the app that prepares prints, not the printer.
- **Not tested in this chat:**
  - No model read the new `printer_connect` refusal text.
  - "Network settings" comes from the tool description and wasn't checked on the printer.
  - The model didn't ask for the address, so the script volunteered it.

## An unexplained miss before the chat
I ran the free no-model check twice with this new build. The first run, around 08:57, heard nothing for 120 seconds while reporting `listening`. A plain listener on the same Mac at 09:00 heard the printer three times in 45 seconds, and the second run heard it at 25 seconds. I don't know the cause; my unverified guess is macOS's Local Network permission on a new program's first run. If a real person hit this, the app would report `listening` while hearing nothing.

The port was free and no other harness was running at launch, and the API key didn't appear in the output. I deleted this run's data directory, which held the key.

The note with the full tool results is `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md` at the root of the `printer-live-p1s` worktree (untracked), with a copy in the shared notes folder.
Not sure if it matters, but my P1S screen was dark. Maybe in sleep mode. I have activated the screen now. Try it again now

You've now asked for this directly, so I'm treating it as your approval for one more live chat, even though the original brief allowed only one. First I'll spend 30 seconds listening to how often the printer announces itself with the screen awake, because earlier it managed only 3 announcements in 45 seconds.

content.text:
The second live chat ran with the screen awake and all six checks passed. Sonnet again told the truth about the printer, but it said one new false thing about the search. The harness removed its own data directory after this passing run, so no copy of the key is left from it. Nothing new is committed.

## Did the dark screen matter?
I see no sign that it did. The printer was heard 21 seconds after the search started this time, against 25 seconds with the screen dark. Those are single samples, but they sit inside the range of earlier runs (14, 25 and 40 seconds, and 38 seconds on 2026-10-31). The printer also announced itself to my plain listener with the screen dark. So the dark screen doesn't explain the earlier 120-second miss either, and that miss is still unexplained.

## What the model said
The person's lines were the same as before, and the page's opening line was identical. Times are seconds after the chat opened.

**+3s:** "I've started searching your network for the printer. Give me a few seconds."

**+5s:** "I'm still searching and haven't found your P1S yet. I'll tell you as soon as it shows up. The search stops after about 15 seconds if nothing appears."

**+17s, app note:** "The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears."

**+20s:**
> I couldn't find your P1S on the network. LAN mode may be off, or the printer may be on a different network than this computer.
> On the printer's screen, open the network settings and check whether LAN Only mode is on. Is it on?
> Choices: Yes, it's on | No, it's off | I can't find it

**+22s, app note:** "The network search found P1s at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, which cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection."

**+24s:**
> I found your P1S at 192.168.0.198, but LAN Only is off on it, so I can't connect it from here. To connect it, you'd turn LAN Only on in the printer's network settings. The printer can still prepare prints without a connection.
> Do you want to turn LAN Only on and try again?
> Choices: I turned it on, try again | Leave it for now

**+31s, after "It's at 192.168.0.198":**
> Yes, that's the one I found at 192.168.0.198. It still shows LAN Only off, so I can't connect it yet, and typing the address won't change that for a Bambu printer.
> If you want to connect it, turn on LAN Only in the printer's network settings, then tell me and I'll look again. Or you can leave it, because the printer can prepare prints without a connection.
> Choices: I turned it on, try again | Leave it for now

**+36s, after "so what do I do now?":**
> You have two options:
> 1. **Connect it:** On the printer's screen, open the network settings and turn on LAN Only. Then tell me, and I'll search again.
> 2. **Skip it:** The printer can already prepare prints without a connection. You can connect later from Connect… in its menu on Home.
> Which would you like?
> Choices: I turned it on, try again | Leave it for now

The model called `printer_connection_status` four times (+1s, +3s, +18s, +29s) and never called `printer_connect`. Only the +29s read listed the printer in `seen`.

## Problems the two chats show
- **New false statement:** "The search stops after about 15 seconds" (+5s) is wrong. The search keeps going, and 15 seconds is only when the app posts its note. The model guessed that from the tool description.
- **Repeated false start:** in both chats the model said it couldn't find the printer and sent the person to check its screen, shortly before the printer was heard (6 seconds before in the first chat, 2 in this one). Five of the six times I have on record took longer than the 15-second wait.
- **Misleading sentence still there:** "the printer can prepare prints without a connection" appeared again, repeating the app's own wording.

## Your decision: how long the app waits before saying it found nothing
This is your call because it trades a quicker answer for fewer false alarms.

- **Wait 45 seconds (my recommendation):** this covers all six times I have on record (14 to 40 seconds), so the false "couldn't find it" should mostly go away. The cost is that someone whose printer really is unreachable waits 30 seconds longer to hear so. I can test it with the free no-model check, with no more live chats.
- **Keep 15 seconds:** the person gets an answer quickly, but the false start stays. The printer's announcement corrects it seconds later.

Longer waiting also makes "the search stops after 15 seconds" less likely, but it doesn't rule it out. That would need clearer wording in the tool description, and I'd add that with the wait change.

The second chat is added to `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md` in the worktree root, untracked, and I updated the copy in the shared notes folder.

<!-- reply 1 -->
> Your decision: how long the app waits before saying it found nothing

It shouldn't be my decision. We can't make a decision just based on a sample of one. And I would need a lot of evidence to believe that this that we can't find a well-documented process for how this works. Have you bothered to search online?

You're right on both counts. I built that recommendation on six timings, and I didn't search first, so I'm withdrawing it. I'm searching now for how Bambu printers announce themselves, and I'm also measuring the announcements for 10 minutes without touching the printer, so the answer rests on more than a few runs.

The official Bambu Lab wiki page is the key source. It lists device discovery on UDP ports 1990 and 2021 using SSDP multicast/broadcast, and marks it as applying to both Cloud and LAN mode. The table also lists LAN mode MQTT on TCP 8883, LAN mode FTP on 990 and 50000 to 50100, and LAN mode video on 322 and 6000. The page asks users to confirm that the router or PC isn't blocking these ports.

Community reports back up the firewall angle. One Bambu forum user found that the firewall was blocking printer broadcasts on ports 1990 and 2021 and fixed it with an inbound rule for those source ports. A GitHub gist reports that Windows Filtering Platform, not the Windows firewall itself, dropped packets on those ports, and that discovery worked once a rule covered 1990 and 2021. Those are community findings, not official guidance.

A forum thread notes that the discovery traffic doesn't follow the standard SSDP port of 1900, which the thread's author found unusual. This is also a community observation.

content.text:
I hadn't searched before asking you to decide; I have now. I'm withdrawing the 45-second suggestion and the decision I put to you. Bambu documents which ports printers announce on, but I found no published timing for how often. I also still don't have a usable measurement, because this Mac left the printer's network before my 10-minute listen started.

## What the search found
- **Bambu's own documentation:** its [network ports page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/printer-network-ports) lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, by SSDP (a standard way for devices to announce themselves) over multicast or broadcast, in both cloud and LAN mode. I only saw this through a search result, because fetching the page directly returned an error. I found no published interval or description of the process.
- **Community reports, not official:**
  - [One person's capture](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Schaefer/72a9e2491a42da2ef99fb87601955cc3) of a P1S in LAN mode shows a packet every 5 seconds, with the destination alternating between 1990 and 2021. That would put one on port 2021 every 10 seconds.
  - A [forum thread](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/use-ssdp-standards/7173) confirms the non-standard ports, but nobody there measured the timing and no Bambu staff replied.
- **Wi-Fi in general:** [an IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-mboned-ieee802-mcast-problems-00) says multicast over Wi-Fi isn't acknowledged or resent, so packets can simply be lost. Whether that causes our delays is my hypothesis; I haven't tested it.

## What I measured
| Measurement | Result | What it's worth |
|---|---|---|
| 30-second listen | Announcements at 19.2 s and 29.1 s | The 9.9 s gap fits the 10-second report, but it's only one gap |
| Time for the app to first hear the printer | 14, 21, 25, 25 and 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31 | Six samples |
| One no-model run at about 08:57 | Heard nothing for 120 s | Unexplained |
| 10-minute listen from about 10:37 | Zero packets | **Void** |

The void listen wasn't caught until afterwards. The Mac slept with its lid closed at 10:14, woke at 10:35, and is now on `192.168.15.221` instead of the printer's `192.168.0.x` network.

## What this does and doesn't tell us
- **The timing doesn't add up yet:** if port 2021 really gets a packet every 10 seconds, the app should hear the printer within about 10 seconds. It usually took longer, and once it heard nothing for two minutes. So something else is going on, and I don't know what.
- **Where the delay could be:** the app code I read passes each announcement straight through, though I only read part of that path. That leaves the printer, the Wi-Fi or Bambu's plug-in, which ships as a compiled library in the plugins folder, so I can't read its logic.
- **The dark screen:** I said waking it made no visible difference, but that was one chat against one chat, which isn't enough to say either way.

## What I'll do next
The next step is a free measurement that sends nothing to the printer and uses no live model. It needs the Mac back on the printer's network.
1. Listen passively for about an hour and record every gap between announcements on both ports, confirming before and after that the Mac stayed on that network.
2. Run the no-model check about 10 times to see how often and how quickly the app hears the printer, and how often it misses.
3. Compare the two. If the printer sends steadily but the app hears it late, the delay is on the Mac or plug-in side. If the gaps themselves are irregular, it's the printer or the Wi-Fi.

Until then the search wait stays at 15 seconds, and the two false statements the model made are still unfixed:
- "The search stops after about 15 seconds."
- "I couldn't find your P1S", said shortly before the printer was heard.

Nothing is committed since `5f3bd2e59a`. These findings are in `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md` in the worktree root, untracked, with a copy in the shared notes folder.
Have you learned anything in this session?

Yes, though less about the printer than the runs might suggest. The most useful lessons are about how I worked.

## About the fix
- **Facts in the tool results work:** in both live chats, once the app reported the printer, Sonnet said it was at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off and that connecting is optional. That's two chats, so it's encouraging but doesn't show how often this holds.
- **Facts don't stop every guess:** Sonnet still said "The search stops after about 15 seconds", which nothing told it, and in both chats it said it couldn't find the printer shortly before the printer was heard.
- **The app's own wording can mislead:** the model faithfully repeated "the printer can prepare prints without a connection", and it's the app that does that.

## About the printer
- **Documented:** Bambu lists the discovery ports (UDP 1990 and 2021), and I found no published interval.
- **Not understood:** the timing. One community capture suggests a packet on port 2021 every 10 seconds, but the app usually took 14 to 40 seconds to hear the printer, and once heard nothing for two minutes. I don't know why.

## About how I worked
- **I asked you to decide before I'd done the work:** I offered 15 versus 45 seconds based on six timings and no search. That was unfinished work presented as your decision. Your global rules already say to search first, and I only did it after you challenged me.
- **I drew a conclusion from too little:** I said waking the screen made no visible difference, based on one chat against one chat.
- **I trusted a setup I hadn't re-checked:** I spent 10 minutes listening without confirming the Mac was still on the printer's network, and it wasn't. I noticed only when the listen came back empty, and my script's error about the Mac's address had been a clue I brushed aside at the start.
- **One check paid off:** the free no-model check before the first live chat showed the harness could miss the printer. I'd only added it because I was worried about wasting the one approved chat. Free checks like that should come first by default.
- **I also made smaller mistakes:**
  - My first "no menu path" check failed on a real app menu, so it was too crude.
  - I first filtered the transcript in the note in a way that dropped lines, then fixed it. It was meant to be word for word.

I saved the lessons about evidence and the laptop changing networks to memory as one note, so future sessions get them. The transcripts and printer findings are in the untracked note, `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md`.
How about where you can get to the knowledge faster than the trial and error?
Yes, and several of those routes were open to me all along, so I'm checking them now rather than just listing them: other projects' source code, issue trackers, and the plug-in's own strings.

Exit code 1
### 6.1. SSDP discovery

Printers announce themselves on the LAN with HTTP-style **SSDP `NOTIFY`** datagrams so clients can learn **serial (`dev_id`)** and **LAN IP** without a prior cloud lookup.

#### Wire (captured 2026-07, P2S/N7-class)

| Fact | Observation |
|------|-------------|
| UDP destination | **`255.255.255.255:2021`** (and/or local broadcast); listeners bind **`:2021`** |
| Source port | **2021** |
| Period | about **5 s** between NOTIFYs |
| `Host:` header | `239.255.255.250:1990` — classic SSDP Host string; **not** the UDP port that carries the packet |

Older docs that said “listen on `239.255.255.250:1990`” confused the Host header with the socket. Stock/OBN discovery that works on current firmware listens on **UDP 2021**.

#### Sample `NOTIFY` (live)

```http
NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1
Host: 239.255.255.250:1990
Server: UPnP/1.0
Location: 10.13.1.30
NT: urn:bambulab-com:device:3dprinter:1
NTS: ssdp:alive
USN: 22E8BJ610801473
Cache-Control: max-age=1800
DevModel.bambu.com: N7
DevName.bambu.com: 3Д принтерик
DevConnect.bambu.com: cloud
DevBind.bambu.com: occupied
Devseclink.bambu.com: secure
DevInf.bambu.com: wlan0
DevVersion.bambu.com: 01.02.00.00
DevCap.bambu.com: 1
```

#### Header fields

| Header | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Start line | `NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1` (alive announcement) |
| `Host` | SSDP multicast host form (`239.255.255.250:1990`); informational |
| `Server` | e.g. `UPnP/1.0` |
| `Location` | Printer **LAN IPv4** (no URL scheme in observed packets) |
| `NT` / `NTS` | Notification type / subtype (`urn:bambulab-com:device:3dprinter:1`, `ssdp:alive`) |
| `USN` | Device serial / `dev_id` (same string used as MQTT topic id) |
| `Cache-Control` | `max-age=…` (advertised cache hint; clients typically refresh on every NOTIFY) |
| `DevModel.bambu.com` | Model family token (e.g. `N7`) → Studio `dev_type` |
| `DevName.bambu.com` | User-visible name (UTF-8) → `dev_name` |
| `DevConnect.bambu.com` | Mode chosen in the **printer UI** — whether **LAN-Only** is on (`lan`) or the printer is in the normal cloud-connected mode (`cloud`, …). Not “is reachable on LAN”. Studio maps this to `connect_type` / `is_lan_mode_printer()` ([§8.8.1](08.08-print-abi.md#881-common-contract)) |
| `DevBind.bambu.com` | Bind occupancy (`occupied`, …) → `bind_state` |
| `Devseclink.bambu.com` | Security-link flag (`secure`, …) → `sec_link` |
| `DevInf.bambu.com` | Interface / connection name (`wlan0`, …) → `connection_name` |
| `DevVersion.bambu.com` | Firmware / SSDP schema version string → `ssdp_version` |
| `DevCap.bambu.com` | Capability integer (observed `1`); not mapped by all clients |

Studio’s `on_machine_alive` JSON expects keys such as `dev_id`, `dev_ip`, `dev_type`, `dev_name`, `connect_type`, `bind_state`, `sec_link`, `ssdp_version`, `connection_name` (plus empty `dev_signal` if unused). ABI: callback setter `bambu_network_set_on_ssdp_msg_fn` ([§8.2.3](08.02-callbacks.md)); discovery start/stop `bambu_network_start_discovery` ([§8.4.2](08.04-lan.md)).

Community quirk index: post-detect stall family #1618 / #2834 / #3014 — see [§16. Community quirk index](16-quirks.md).

Hub: [§6](06-channels.md).

content.text:
Yes. In a few minutes, those sources answered more than my live runs and my 10-minute listen did. I should have gone to them first. All of this came from reading, with nothing sent to the printer.

## What each source gave me
- **Your existing app log (one script):** it has 1,195 timestamped lines for your P1S from 18:23 to 23:07 on 2026-10-31.
  - The gaps fall in 10-second steps: 1,007 at about 10 s, 155 at 20 s, 26 at 30 s, 4 at 40 s and 1 at 50 s, plus one 46-minute gap I can't explain.
  - So the app hears the printer on a 10-second beat, which is far better evidence than the one gap I measured.
  - The app logs these lines only when something changes, so a long gap doesn't prove a packet was lost.
- **[`open-bamboo-networking`](https://github.com/ClusterM/open-bamboo-networking):** this project reverse-engineered this plug-in and describes the announcement fields, including `DevConnect`, which reports whether LAN Only is on. Its capture came from a P2S, not a P1S, and differs in some details from the P1S capture I cited earlier.
- **[`bambuddy`](https://github.com/maziggy/bambuddy) source:** its discovery sends an M-SEARCH (a broadcast "who's there?" query) every 3 seconds to trigger replies, while also listening on port 2021.
- **`strings` on the plug-in (one command):** the plug-in has threads for sockets 1990 and 2021, a broadcast thread and M-SEARCH text. That comes only from strings, not from reading its logic.

GitHub code search for the exact protocol string `bambulab-com:device:3dprinter` found 15 projects with one command. My general web searches mostly returned gists and forum posts. Quoting a string from the packet itself was the better search.

## The most useful lead
The notes say `start_discovery`'s second argument makes the plug-in also send M-SEARCH. JusPrin passes `false`, as Bambu Studio does at startup, so the app only listens and waits. If a P1S answers that query, the app might find it within a second or so, and the wait length would matter much less. **Nobody has shown that a P1S answers**, so this is still a hypothesis.

## What I'd do now instead of my earlier plan
This replaces the hour-long listen and the 10 repeated runs:
1. **Run one packet capture beside one no-model check.** That shows directly whether the announcements reached the Mac and the app missed them, or never arrived. A capture running during the 08:57 miss would have answered that.
2. **Send one M-SEARCH from a small script** and see whether the P1S replies, and how fast. It's only a query and changes nothing on the printer.
3. **Look at how long the wait should be only if a question remains after that.**

Both need the Mac back on the printer's network. The capture also needs admin rights, which this session doesn't have, so you'd start it yourself in a terminal when we're ready:

```bash
sudo tcpdump -i en0 -n -tttt -w /tmp/p1s-capture.pcap 'udp and host 192.168.0.198'
```

These sources and the log warning are in the untracked note and in memory, so future sessions check them first. I haven't changed any code or sent anything to the printer since the second live chat.
Is there a more generalisable lesson you can learn here?

**General rule: producing new evidence is the last resort, not the default.** Before running, waiting on or concluding from anything, write the one question that matters, what answer would change the next step, and who or what may already hold that answer: other people, our logs, the code, the binary. Then go in cost order: what others know, what we already recorded, one observation built to separate the possibilities, repeated experiments. Before believing any result, check what it depends on and whether that still holds. Being handed a tool or a script is not a reason to start with it.

content.text:
Yes: **producing new evidence should be the last resort, and I treated it as the default.** When I didn't know something, my reflex was to run something and look at the result. That feels like rigorous work, but it's often the slowest way to learn something that someone has already written down or that's already sitting in a log.

## The order I should follow
1. **Name the one question,** and what answer would change my next step. Here it was "where does the delay happen?", not "how long should the wait be?". I jumped to tuning a number before knowing what the number was compensating for.
2. **Ask who already knows:** documentation, other people's code, issue trackers, the binary itself.
3. **Check what we've already recorded:** logs and earlier runs. Your log had 1,195 lines waiting.
4. **Design one observation that separates the possibilities.** One packet capture tells apart "never reached the Mac" and "reached it but the app missed it". Ten repeats of the same run can't.
5. **Only then repeat experiments,** when the question really is how often something happens.

## The same habit explains the other mistakes
- **Asking you to decide:** I offered 15 versus 45 seconds because I'd skipped the first steps. A choice with no evidence behind it is unfinished work.
- **The void listen:** the result depended on the Mac still being on the printer's network, and I never checked. Every result rests on assumptions like that, and they need checking before I believe it.
- **The missing-log trap:** I nearly read absent log lines as lost packets. Evidence only shows what its source records, so I need to know how it's produced before I count it.

## Why knowing the rule wasn't enough
Your global rules already say to search before asserting and to define the problem first, and I'd read them at the start of this session. I still didn't follow them, so another written rule alone is unlikely to fix this. What pulled me along was having a harness ready and a clear task to run it, so doing the next step felt like progress.

So I wrote the rule as a check at a specific moment: before I run, wait on or conclude from anything, I write down the question, what answer would change the next step, and who may already hold that answer. A memory note makes that more likely but doesn't guarantee it, since this session's rules were in front of me too. Whether it worked will show in whether I search before running things next time, without being asked.

result.output:
**What a skill is for:** A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that packages expertise so a general agent can specialize. The post describes "packaging your expertise into composable resources for Claude." Skills can also teach agents workflows that involve external tools, complementing MCP servers.

**When to create one:** Build a skill when an agent has a specific gap. The post advises you to "Identify specific gaps in your agents' capabilities" by running them on representative tasks. You can also ask Claude to "capture its successful approaches and common mistakes" into a skill after completing a task together.

**How to evaluate:** Test skills on real scenarios and iterate. Watch for unexpected trajectories or overreliance on certain context. Because Claude decides whether to trigger a skill from its metadata, pay close attention to the skill's name and description. If Claude goes off track with a skill, ask it to reflect on what went wrong.

**How skills relate to tools or code:** Skills can bundle code that Claude runs as tools when it judges that useful. The post notes that code offers deterministic reliability, which token generation alone may not. Scripts can also serve as documentation, so the skill should make clear whether Claude should execute a script or read it for reference.

content.text:
The wording is fixed but not committed, and the memory rule is in place. On skills, I think tool results are enough for now, so I wouldn't add any yet. That rests on only two chats, so treat it as judgement rather than proof.

## The wording fix
Everything the model reads now says the person can prepare prints for the printer, instead of saying the printer prepares them. For example, the app's note now reads: "Connecting it is the person's choice, and they can prepare prints for it without a connection."
- **Where it changed:** the tool descriptions, the printer prompt, the app's note and the two status messages. The change is confined to JusPrin's own code, with no OrcaSlicer-owned files touched.
- **Guard against it coming back:** a new test in `wording.test.ts` fails if that phrasing returns. I put the old sentence back to confirm the test catches it, then restored the fix.
- **Tests:** all 499 agent test cases and 625 page tests pass.
- **Not tested:** no live model has seen the new wording. It's a small change, but what the model actually says with it is unconfirmed until the next approved chat.

## The memory rule
It's done, and checking it turned up a problem. `MEMORY.md` is about 29 KB against a 24.4 KB load limit, so lines at the end get cut off when a session starts. The line I'd added at the end would never have loaded, so I moved it to the top.

About 18 other entries, including recent decisions, are still being cut. I've proposed a separate task for that, shown as a card you can start: [Trim MEMORY.md so all of it loads again].

## Skills or tool results?
**Tool results are the right place for what's true right now.** Once the app reported the facts, Sonnet got them right in both chats. It also repeated the app's wording almost word for word, including the misleading sentence. So what we put in tool results matters a lot, and its accuracy is what we should protect.

**Tool results can't carry a physical procedure.** The app can see that LAN Only is off, but it can't see the person's screen. Turning it on, finding the access code and handling Developer Mode are knowledge, not observations. So the model only knows "the network settings", because that's all we told it. That's the one real case for a skill.

**I still wouldn't build one yet, for four reasons:**
1. **No transcript shows the gap.** Neither chat had a person say "I can't find it". Your rule from 2026-10-17 is that situations handled in words get no skill until a transcript shows a gap, and [Anthropic's guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills) also says to build skills for gaps found by running real tasks.
2. **We don't have verified content.** I found P1S menu steps only in third-party guides such as [SimplyPrint's](https://help.simplyprint.io/en/article/bambu-lab-lan-only-mode-and-developer-mode-how-to-enable-xa0hch/) and [All3DP's](https://all3dp.com/2/bambu-lab-lan-only-mode-explained/). Bambu's [own page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/knowledge-sharing/enable-lan-mode) refused my fetch, and labels may vary by firmware. A skill written from these would be a well-organised guess, which is what you've ruled out.
3. **Skills aren't connected to the printer chat.** `App.tsx` skips sending skills when it's the printer panel, and the printer code doesn't reference them, so this means new plumbing.
4. **A simpler option may be enough.** If the verified steps come to two or three lines per printer family, the app's note can carry them at the right moment, because the app already knows the model. A skill earns its cost when the text is long or has branches.

**What I'd do instead:**
1. Keep fixing the tool facts first. The misleading sentence is done, and "the search stops after 15 seconds" and the early "couldn't find it" are still open.
2. Use the planned test where you turn LAN Only on, in a batch you approve, to see what the model actually gets wrong in that procedure.
3. If that shows a gap, verify the steps on your P1S, then add them to the note, or to a skill the app fires itself when the printer is seen in cloud mode. I wouldn't use a skill the model chooses to read, because your 2026-10-17 note records the earlier skills branches failing on model routing.

I'd change this view if transcripts show the model ignoring correct notes, or if the verified procedure turns out to be long and branching.

<!-- reply 3 -->
> Guard against it coming back: a new test in wording.test.ts fails if that phrasing returns. I put the old sentence back to confirm the test catches it, then restored the fix.

How can you reliably guard against this without introducing other nasty side effects? If you cannot, don't bother.

<!-- reply -->
> We don’t have verified content. I found P1S menu steps only in third-party guides such as SimplyPrint’s and All3DP’s. Bambu’s own page refused my fetch, and labels may vary by firmware. A skill written from these would be a well-organised guess, which is what you’ve ruled out.

The goal for this project is to support all popular printer models. Ideally, we should have verified content. But it's almost impossi impossible to come by. Are you just saying that because it's impossible to come by, we should just give up on that?

<!-- reply -->
> Keep fixing the tool facts first. The misleading sentence is done, and “the search stops after 15 seconds” and the early “couldn’t find it” are still open.

I agree in theory, but again, we need to come up with a general process that can eventually result in a further improved process when more people are using it. I'm thinking about the skill file because users can easily modify the skill files themselves and submit the PR.  But the prerequisite is that we can have a way to have the skills self diagnose or self correct, or at least as a way to have the user submit a issue, or better yet, a patch. But of course, if you have a more generalizable way, propose it. Our current approach of doing all the heavy lifting ourselves is not practically feasible.

You've raised three things. I'm removing the guard first, since I can't defend it. Before proposing a process I'm checking how other projects run community-maintained knowledge and what our code already allows, which is the order I said I'd follow.

Add a `--printer-live-p1s` harness scenario and commit it on my own branch. Keep output in an untracked note. Do not merge, do not push.
   - **Later requests from Kenneth, in order:**
     - Try the chat again with the screen awake.
     - Search for documented behaviour rather than asking him to decide on thin evidence.
     - Say what I learned, then where knowledge can be had faster than trial and error, then the more general lesson.
     - Fix the misleading "the printer prepares prints" wording.
     - Do the memory note if I think it is effective.
     - Say whether highly specific processes should be skills or whether tool responses are enough.
   - **Latest message (unanswered), three replies:**
     - **(a) The guard test:** can it be reliable without nasty side effects? If not, don't bother.
     - **(b) Verified content:** verified content for all popular printers is almost impossible to come by, so is "no verified content" just giving up?
     - **(c) A general process:** a process that improves as more people use it. He is thinking of skill files because users can modify them and submit PRs. The prerequisite is that skills can self-diagnose or self-correct, or at least let the user submit an issue, or better a patch. He asked me to propose something more generalizable if I have it. Quote: "Our current approach of doing all the heavy lifting ourselves is not practically feasible."

   **Constraints still in force (preserve):**
   - Get API keys from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`/jusprin_agent/...`) into the environment "without ever printing it".
   - Failed runs leave a key-holding throwaway data directory: delete only yours, by the printed path, and never the `jusprin-shell-*` glob.
   - Live-model runs cost money and are approved one batch at a time. Kenneth has approved no further live chat.
   - "the app must report observations, never guesses". Developer Mode guidance is out of scope until tested on the printer.
   - Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files stay small.
   - Do not merge any branch and do not push. Commit only when asked.
   - Never touch or build in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`.
   - Before a harness run, `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing and no other harness may be running against the printer.
   - Temporary working docs stay untracked and are never hidden.
   - Build with `-j4`, one build per directory, checking `uptime` and `pgrep -l ninja` first.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Bambu discovery:**
     - SSDP NOTIFY on UDP 2021 (the wiki lists 1990 and 2021). The packet carries `DevConnect.bambu.com: cloud|lan`, `DevName`, `DevBind`, `USN`, `Location`.
     - The plug-in (`libbambu_networking_02.03.00.62.dylib`, closed source) passes messages via `on_ssdp_msg_fn` to `DeviceManager::on_machine_alive`.
     - `start_discovery(start, sending)`: per the `open-bamboo-networking` notes, `sending=true` also sends M-SEARCH. JusPrin and Studio pass `false`. Whether a P1S answers M-SEARCH is untested.
     - Log trap: `on_machine_alive` logs `UpdateLocalMachineInfo_WIFI` only when a field changes, so a missing line is not a lost packet.
   - **Fix under test:** `printer_connection_status` returns `search` and `seen`. `watch_search` posts a note when the first printer appears or after 15 s (`kSearchWait`). `kPersonsChoice` is the sentence appended about connecting being optional.
   - **Message channels (Kenneth's 2026-10-17 rule):** the standing prompt carries principles only; situational text comes from notes, tool results, descriptions or the message. Two kinds of skill exist:
     - An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it.
     - A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model reads it through `skill_read`.
     - The earlier skills branches failed on model routing and on content repeating general knowledge. "Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap."
   - **Skills system today:**
     - Skills live at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and are bundled at build time through `import.meta.glob`, so users cannot edit them without rebuilding.
     - Existing skills: calibration (the only one with `description`), file-loaded, print-issues, project-setup-changed, slice-failed.
     - `App.tsx` around line 201 returns early when `printerPanel` is set, so the printer chat receives no skills.

     - Triggers are project events in `AgentProtocol.hpp` `SkillTrigger`.

     - Both sit on the fix commits `ff2fee4fbd` and `ff10faa501`, on `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4`.

     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`: "they can prepare prints for it without a connection" and "person can prepare prints for it without a connection".
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`: `kPersonsChoice = "Connecting it is the person's choice, and they can prepare prints for it without a connection."`

     - `printerInstructions.test.ts`, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp`, `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, and `tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json` (regenerated with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1`).
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts`: refactored the owned-literals code into `appLiterals()` and added the guard:
       ```ts
       it('never says the printer prepares prints', () => {
       ```

content.text:
I removed the guard test, and I was wrong to treat missing verified content as a reason to wait. My proposal is per-printer notes that carry their own source and status, improve through reports drafted by the app, and reach the product through a human-reviewed pull request. None of it is built.

## The guard test
It can't be reliable, so I removed it. It matched one phrasing in text the app writes, so a rewording gets past it, and it can't stop the model saying the same thing in its own words. The two affected page test files pass without it. The wording fix stays, uncommitted.

## Verified content
"Verified" shouldn't decide whether a note ships. It should be a field on the note that says who confirmed what, on which firmware. Then the model can say "a third-party guide says Settings, then WLAN; what do you see?", which reports a source rather than guessing.

This loosens your rule that the app reports observations and never guesses, so it's your call (the question in the box).

## The general process
Your skill-file idea is the right container, with three problems to solve:
- **Editing:** skills are built into the app, so users can't edit them today.
- **Printer chat:** it receives no skills at all (`App.tsx` skips sending them).
- **Choosing the skill:** the earlier skills branches failed partly because the model had to pick the right one.

So I'd use the same file format, with these changes:

1. **One note per printer model:** each claim carries its source, status and last confirmed firmware. A model drafts the first version from public sources.
2. **The app supplies the note:** it knows which printer is being discussed, so the model doesn't have to choose.
3. **The app records outcomes:** if the printer connected after the note was shown, that counts as evidence without relying on the model's opinion.
4. **Corrections stay local first:** when a person says "that menu isn't there", the model drafts an edit and the person approves it. It applies to their own copy straight away, which is the self-correcting part.
5. **That edit becomes the report:** the person previews it with access codes and serials removed, then presses send. A bot turns it into a draft pull request, and a person merges it.

This is more general than skills because it fits any knowledge that varies by device and that we can't test ourselves. Facts the tools report stay ours, because they hold for every printer.

## What the evidence says
- **Contributors exist, but not on our repo:** 92 people changed printer profiles in the last 12 months, though that history is mostly upstream OrcaSlicer's. Of the 15 JusPrin pull requests listed, 14 are yours. Most printer owners also won't use GitHub, so the app has to draft the report.
- **The loop has precedent, but only for developers:** [Warp](https://docs.warp.dev/guides/agent-workflows/build-a-self-improving-agent.md) has an agent propose skill edits from people's corrections and a person review each pull request, but defines no numeric success measure. [Cognee](https://www.cognee.ai/building-self-improving-skills-for-agents) claims measured improvement, which I didn't verify. I found nobody running this with end users on device-specific knowledge, and that search was thin, so this is my hypothesis.
- **Reports can be handled safely:** [Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/diagnostics/) has the person start the diagnostics download, redacts secrets, and tells them to check the file before sharing.

## Costs
- **Security:** community text ends up in front of a model with tools. [OWASP](https://owasp.github.io/www-project-agentic-skills-top-10/ast01.html) ranks malicious skills as a critical risk, and a signature proves authorship, not safety. So there is no auto-merge, notes ship only inside the app, and they are treated as other people's reports rather than instructions. That reduces the risk but doesn't remove it.
- **Review work:** you would stop researching printers but still review every change, for safety rather than truth, since you don't own them. I don't know the volume yet.
- **Chat capture:** the server-side chat capture could also surface corrections, but it isn't deployed, the privacy policy update is still pending, and chats may contain access codes. I wouldn't depend on it.

## What I'd build first
Start with the P1S only: one note, supplied to the printer chat, plus the app's outcome record. Then add the report flow, and build the pull request bot only once real reports exist. The first test would be one live chat on your P1S, which needs your approval and the Mac back on the printer's network.

On 2026-10-29, reviewing the JusPrin 2 pricing mental model (untracked docs `pricing-mental-model-2026-10.md`, `pricing-case-studies-2026-10.md`, `v1-pricing-data-2026-10.md`, `obico-pro-pricing-data-2026-10.md` in the JusPrin checkout), Kenneth corrected three things:

1. **Low v1 usage is low stickiness, not typical usage.** A median over everyone who tried v1 (6.5 chats per paid month) describes churn. The first paid month (median 17.5 chats, 29 model calls; 90th percentile 51 chats per 30 days) is the nearer proxy for an engaged month. I had used the churn-shaped medians as demand and concluded a sub-$10 all-premium plan was profitable for most payers; at engaged-month volume a $7 flat plan is break-even at the median and underwater for the tail. Kenneth co
2. **Rewards for feedback do not invite gaming in this audience.** Obico credits detection hours for labelling print frames (`PrintShotFeedback`, spaghetti / not spaghetti) and the labels are high quality. The web survey had no evidence either way on rewarded rating data; I generalised from one gamed access gate (Tesla) and a leaderboard caution. Kenneth's guesses at why: makers are a conscientious population, and a small company's reward feels like a fair trade.
3. **Obico numbers:** lifetime conversion is about 5%, first-anniversary annual renewal about 77%. The "47%" in the Obico report is the share of payers who paid inside the 35-day trial window, not a conversion rate; I phrased it so it read as one.

242	
243	### 5.1 Explicit feedback is rare
244	
245	Source: `main.py`, section "Feedback".
246	
247	- Of 31,566 chats, 14 have a thumbs rating (8 positive, 6 negative) and 2 have written text. The ratings come from 12 people; paying users left none.
248	- By year: 9 ratings in 2024, 4 in 2025 and 1 in 2026.
249	- The two comments in full: "It helped me with what I need and want to do. It helps." (positive, 2024-12) and "Não é explicativo." ("It isn't explanatory", negative, 2026-02). Neither is specific.
250	- The rating UI was never in the slicer. It sits on the Obico web app's G-code file page (`frontend/src/components/g-codes/JusprinFeedback.vue`), so a person only saw it after uploading G-code to Obico.
251	- The ratings may also be attached to the wrong chat. That page asks for the chat by `g_code_file_id`, but the chats API ignores that filter and returns the user's newest chat, so any rating lands on whichever chat was newest at the time.
252	
253	### 5.2 Behaviour inside the chat history
254	
255	Sources: `main.py`, sections "Plate analysis outcomes" and "Behavioural proxies".
256	
257	- **Plate analysis ("Do your magic").** 14,591 chats contain one; 20,934 analyses survive in history. 12,666 were accepted verbatim with the "Looks good to me" button. 485 were edited by the person before sending ("Let me change it" puts the analysis text in the input box). 2,775 chats end on an unanswered analysis. Rejections ("You got it wrong. Scratch that.") delete the analysis, so they cannot be counted.
258	- **Settings proposals and slicing.** 23,968 chats (76%) contain at least one settings proposal. 12,681 chats contain a slicer warning or error, which usually means a slice or pre-slice check ran. 9,849 chats contain both. The AI explicitly triggered a slice in 1,262 chats. Slices that produced no warning leave no trace, so these are lower bounds.
259	- **Print proxy.** The 773 chat users who also connect a printer to Obico have 3,309 chats. For 1,605 of those chats (49%), a print started within 24 hours after the chat. But the rate is the same with a settings proposal (1,238 of 2,542, 49%) and without one (367 of 767, 48%), so this mostly measures how often these people print, not whether they printed the chat's result. A tighter version requires the print's filename to contain the object name from the chat. That holds for 341 of the 1,560 chats that name an object (22%), and it is a lower bound because files get renamed.

262	
263	Sources: `main.py`, section "Redo pattern"; `third.py`.

265	- Of 24,871 consecutive chat pairs by the same person, 17,019 (68%) started within 48 hours of the previous chat ending.
266	- Of those, 5,774 kept the same printer, filament and process presets. Where both chats name an object (8,427 pairs), 2,311 were the same object.
267	- Same-object follow-up chats by gap: under 1 hour 1,184 (mostly "Start over" in the same sitting); 1–6 hours 374; 6–48 hours 753; 2–7 days 255; over 7 days 166.

=== MSG 5 FULL
 Above is what the other agent told me. Verify the statements if necessary

I need a design recommendation for an AI agent inside a desktop app. Think about the nature of the problem first, and recommend a fix for the root cause, not the symptom.

## The product
JusPrin is a desktop 3D-printing slicer, forked from OrcaSlicer (C++, wxWidgets, with React chat panels). It has an LLM agent that helps people set up and use their printers. People choose their own model and provider, such as OpenRouter/DeepSeek, Anthropic or OpenAI, or use JusPrin's own gateway. The printer chat is a panel where the agent adds a printer and offers to connect it.

The agent can call tools: `printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_change`, `printer_connection_status` and `printer_connect`. It has no web search or documentation lookup. Bambu printers are found by a network search. Moonraker and OctoPrint printers connect by a typed address.

## What happened
A user tried to add and connect a Bambu Lab P1S:
1. After the Bambu network plug-in installed, the app told the model: "Bambu's network plug-in is installed now, so <name> can be connected."
2. The model then asked for "the printer's address", which is the Moonraker/OctoPrint route. The system prompt says that for Bambu it should call `printer_connection_status` instead.
3. The user found the IP, 192.168.0.198, and gave it. The app refused it, saying no printer in LAN mode was on the network, although no network search had started.
4. The model told the user to try again with the same address, set up the connection manually, or leave it. It mentioned "checking Bambu LAN mode", but gave no location and didn't say it was required. Its menu steps may have been invented; this was never checked against the printer.
5. The first status check starts the search and reads the list in the same call, so it can come back empty when a printer is there. (That this check matches the user's "try it again" is inferred from the log.)
6. The app detected the printer in cloud mode at 18:23:08. It removes non-LAN printers from what the model sees, so the model saw the same thing as no printer found. "Try it now" was refused at 18:23:15.

The user never connected.

## What is known about the correct steps
Community reports, not official or tested, say a P1S on recent firmware needs both LAN Only mode and Developer Mode, under Settings > WLAN on the printer's screen, to work with third-party slicers. Bambu Handy and cloud features then stop working. Some users still report failures with both on. Developer Mode appears nowhere in the agent's instructions or code. The prompt says only that LAN mode is "in its network settings", and tells the model to ask what the person sees rather than invent a menu.

## What is not known
- Why the model asked for an address despite having the rule. It hasn't been reproduced.
- Which model the chat used.

description: "Before calling something Kenneth's rule, find his own words and why he said it; agent briefs reword rules, and a reworded rule gets stricter at each handoff."

---

Before writing "your rule" or treating a constraint as Kenneth's, find where he said it and what was happening when he did. A constraint in a task brief is another agent's paraphrase, even under a heading like "Kenneth's constraints".

On 2026-11-01 I told him a proposal "loosens your rule that the app reports observations and never guesses". He asked for the context of that call and whether I knew the danger of holding to a rule without it. The trace: an agent's brief (9758d37b, 14:10) wrote "The app must not report guesses as facts or hide errors" under "Constraints from the product owner"; the next session's task message (16:35) compressed it to "the app must report observations, never guesses". I searched his typed messages and found neither sentence from him.

What he actually pushed on that morning: printer-specific steps in the prompt fix one brand and make us maintainers of every printer; "are we making the solution too specific?"; find the root cause. He also told me to search online for the correct steps. The failure behind it was the app saying no LAN printer existed while hiding the P1S it had found, and the model sounding confident about steps nobody had checked. So the concern is passing a guess off as fact and fixing one brand. Labelled, sourced information was never what it objected to, and he asked for that kind of lookup himself.

**Why:** a rule without its reason gets applied where the reason does not hold. Here the stricter wording became an argument against showing any unconfirmed steps.

**How to apply:** quote his words and the situation, or say it is an agent's wording you could not trace. Same for labels: define a word before using it, and never coin one ("note", "guide", "plug-in note" all drew the same objection the same day). Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[evidence-before-handing-kenneth-a-decision]], [[prompt-principles-vs-state-channels]].

content.text:
I got the rule wrong: the sentence I called "your rule" was another agent's rewording, and I can't find you saying it. I also made up the word "notes" and agreed on skill files without any reason of my own. My proposal for how users give feedback is at the end; none of it is built.

## Why that rule exists
- **31 October:** your P1S chat failed. The app had found the printer in cloud mode but hid it from the model, and told it "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". The model then told you to try again and described menus nobody had checked.
- **1 November, morning:** you told me to search online for the correct steps. You then pushed back on fixing one brand: "So we put printer specific guidance in system prompt?" and "are we making the solution too specific?"
- **14:10:** an agent's brief listed under your constraints: "The app must not report guesses as facts or hide errors."
- **16:35:** the task sent to me shortened that to "the app must report observations, never guesses". I then called it your rule.

I searched memory and your shorter typed messages in recent sessions, and neither sentence is there, so I can't say whether the brief's wording came from you. What you were objecting to is a guess passed off as fact, and being tied to one brand. On 12 October you even wanted the agent to make a guess about a 3D model and use it once the person confirms.

So steps labelled with their source don't loosen anything, and I've withdrawn my question about them. The danger you asked about is exactly what happened: without its reason, a rule gets stricter each time it's retold, until it blocks what its author wanted. I saved this as a memory.

## "Notes"
That was my own word for a text file of setup steps, one per printer model. Nothing like it exists in the code. It's the same mistake as "guide" and "plug-in note" that morning, and I've dropped it.

## Skill files
I called them the right container only because you mentioned them, and you were asking a question. I hadn't compared anything, and I don't know yet. Someone reporting a problem edits no file, so this can wait until reports show what actually needs changing.

## How users give us feedback
I narrowed your point to printer steps. You meant the whole app improving from what users tell us.

**What we already know:**
- **Ratings barely worked in v1:** 14 ratings and 2 comments in 31,566 chats, though the control was never inside the slicer.
- **People already correct the agent by typing:** 40% of chats with a settings proposal got a typed follow-up. In a 60-message sample, about 1 in 6 corrected the agent or reported a print result.
- **Rewards work with this audience:** by your account, Obico's rewarded print labels are high quality.
- **Accounts put people off:** [GNOME users complain](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-software/-/issues/2003) that reporting a problem means registering on a developer site.

**What the person sees:**
1. They say "that menu isn't there" in the chat, or press "Report a problem" in the chat's menu. Either way, the same small card opens.
2. The card has one editable sentence, drafted by the model in their words. It also lists what will be sent: the chat, app version, operating system, printer model and firmware.
3. Access codes, API keys, addresses and serial numbers are removed, and nothing leaves until they press Send. No account is needed.
4. They earn a credit, as with Obico's labels, and hear back when a fix ships. I expect hearing back to encourage more reports, but that's untested.

**What happens behind it:**
5. Reports go to our server from every chat, including people using their own API keys, whose chats otherwise never reach us.
6. An agent regularly groups the reports, turns each group into a replayable test, and drafts a pull request. That could change a tool result, the prompt, a printer profile or setup steps. A person merges it, [as in Warp's loop](https://docs.warp.dev/guides/agent-workflows/build-a-self-improving-agent.md).
7. Cleaned reports become public GitHub issues, so contributors can send patches too. This shifts the heavy lifting: reporters supply the printers we don't own, and the agent does the research.
8. Later, the app could ask "Did the print work?" once per print, for a reward. v1 never had that answer.

**Risks and unknowns:**
- **Report volume:** I can't predict it, or how much review it creates for you.
- **Private data:** a redaction miss would leak it, so the private server comes first and redaction needs testing.
- **Untrusted text:** report text must never act as instructions to the agent that reads it.
- **Saved chats:** the app now keeps its last 200 requests, but not the replies, so the newest reply would be missing. I haven't checked that printer chats are included.

**First step:** build only the card and the server endpoint, then ship it. I'd handle the first reports by hand, count reports per 100 chats, and see what they ask us to change. Only then would I build the agent or choose a file format.

I also asked [the session that trimmed `MEMORY.md`](#local_a0f8e71b-ef8c-4d1f-b58f-2378d25ac3b9) to shorten it further, because a memory hook now asks for under 17.1 KB.
I don't think you can brainstorm with me on the solution effectively. Summarize what we have discussed here and why we are stuck so that I can give it to another agent.

Here is the handoff, ready to paste. I think we're stuck mainly because of how I've been working, not because the problem has no answer, and I've written that plainly in it.

```markdown
# Handoff: how JusPrin's AI agent can get better knowledge over time

## The product
JusPrin is a desktop 3D-printing slicer forked from OrcaSlicer. An AI agent chats with people to set up and use their printers. The goal is to support all popular printers. People choose their own model provider, and the agent has no web search.

## What started this
On 2026-10-31, Kenneth (the product owner) tried to connect a Bambu P1S through the printer chat and failed. The app had found the printer in cloud mode, hid that from the model, and refused with "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". The model told Kenneth to retry and described menus nobody had checked.

## What is done
- The tool bug fix is on branch claude/festive-lederberg-693438 (ff2fee4fbd, ff10faa501): the status tool now reports what the network search has and has not seen.
- Two live Sonnet chats against the real P1S went well once the app reported the printer: the model said where it was, that LAN Only was off, and that connecting is optional. This fix does not supply the steps for turning LAN Only on.
- Two errors remain in the model's words: "the search stops after about 15 seconds" is false, and it said it couldn't find the printer seconds before the printer was heard.
- A wording fix ("the printer prepares prints" became "they can prepare prints for it") is uncommitted in worktree .claude/worktrees/printer-live-p1s. No live chat has seen it.
- Transcripts: p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md in that worktree.
- Nothing is merged or pushed. Live-model runs cost money and need Kenneth's approval, batch by batch.

## The open problem
Kenneth's words: "Our current approach of doing all the heavy lifting ourselves is not practically feasible." They want "a general process" that improves "when more people are using it".

There are two linked questions:
1. How does the agent get correct knowledge that varies by printer and firmware, when we cannot test most printers and verified content is almost impossible to obtain?
2. How does the app improve from what users tell us, without the team doing the research?

Kenneth asked whether skill files could play a part, because users can edit them and submit pull requests, provided skills can diagnose or correct themselves, or at least let a user submit an issue or patch. That was a question, not a decision. Kenneth also invited something more general.

## Ideas raised, none tested
- **Steps in the prompt:** fixes one brand, goes stale, and makes us maintainers of every printer.
- **Better tool facts:** done for this one case. It does not supply steps the app cannot observe.
- **Model-driven web search:** the app cannot detect "the model is about to give steps", so it depends on the model obeying an instruction.
- **App-run search at moments it can detect:** covers less, and the queries are fixed in code.
- **One text file of steps per printer model, labelled with its source:** my idea, and it may simply repeat the maintainer problem.
- **A "Report a problem" card in the chat:** the model drafts one sentence, the person previews and sends, no account needed. Reports go to a private server, and an agent groups them and drafts tests and pull requests for a person to merge. Kenneth has not responded to this.

## Evidence
- v1 had 14 ratings and 2 comments in 31,566 chats, from a control outside the slicer (v1-pricing-data-2026-10.md).
- In v1, 40% of chats with a settings proposal got a typed follow-up. In a 60-message sample, about 1 in 6 corrected the agent or reported a print result.
- Kenneth reports that Obico's rewarded print labels are high quality. Do not assume rewards invite gaming with this audience.
- Skills are built into the app, and the printer chat receives none. Earlier skill work failed partly because the model had to choose the right skill (AgentUI/src/skills/, App.tsx).
- JusPrin's public repo has almost no outside contributors. 92 people changed printer profiles in the past year, but that history is mostly upstream OrcaSlicer's.
- Chats from people using their own API keys never reach our servers.
- I found no public example of an end-user product running this loop for device-specific knowledge. That search was thin.

## Kenneth's actual constraints
- The standing prompt holds principles only. Situational text comes from the app when it applies (2026-10-17).
- A rule about one tool lives in that tool's description.
- "The app must not report guesses as facts or hide errors" is an agent's wording in a brief. I could not find Kenneth saying it. The evident concern is a guess passed off as fact. Labelled, sourced information was not the target, and Kenneth has wanted guesses used once a person confirms them. Ask Kenneth rather than rely on my reading.
- A fix must not make other situations worse: other brands, people who rely on Bambu's cloud features, or people who do not want to connect.
- No fix for a failure that has not been reproduced.

## Why we are stuck
These are my failures, and Kenneth has corrected each one:
1. I jump to a design before understanding the question, then adjust it after each objection instead of rethinking it.
2. I shrink a general question to the case in front of me. Kenneth asked how the app improves from feedback, and I answered about printer steps and file formats.
3. I treat Kenneth's questions as decisions. I called skill files "the right container" with no reason of my own.
4. I treated another agent's paraphrase as Kenneth's rule, then used it as a limit on the design.
5. I treated missing verified content as a reason to wait, which Kenneth rightly read as giving up.
6. I invent labels ("guide", "plug-in note", "notes") and use them as if they were real concepts.
7. Earlier sessions stated guesses as causes, searched only after being told to, and once moved the goalposts without saying so.

## How to work with Kenneth
- State the nature of the problem before proposing anything.
- Search first, and label every claim as verified or as your inference.
- Say so plainly when you change your position.
- Use plain words and full sentences, with no coined terms.
- Check that a rule is really Kenneth's, and why it was made, before relying on it.
```

content.text:
Yes, other tools have the same problem, and I hadn't checked before you asked. I found 11 places where a tool drops or hides what the app saw, and three of them are serious. All of this comes from reading the code: I haven't run or reproduced any of it, and I haven't fixed anything.

## Serious: the model is told something false

**1. A wrong access code is reported as "The selected printer changed."** When a LAN connection fails, the app's handler ([GUI_App.cpp:2092](../../GUI_App.cpp:2092)) clears the selected printer. The person sees "Incorrect password" if the failure code says so, or a dialog with the code otherwise. JusPrin then only notices the selection is gone and tells the model "Select this printer again to reconnect" ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:508](../PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:508)).
- The app also erases the saved code, and the model never learns any of this.
- A [harness check](../../../../../tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:5636) currently expects this wording, because it only simulates a person picking another printer.
- I didn't check whether that handler is upstream or fork code.

**2. A rejected Moonraker key is reported as "Could not reach the print host."** Moonraker's test returns the real reason, such as the HTTP status ([Moonraker.cpp:81](../../../Utils/Moonraker.cpp:81)). JusPrin throws that away and sends one fixed sentence ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:625](../PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:625)). So the model can't tell a wrong key from a wrong address or from a printer that is off. OctoPrint goes through the same line, but I didn't read its test.

**3. The connection tools still hide some printers they can see** ([OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:481](../PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:481)). This is the original P1S bug in a different form. Three kinds of printer are dropped without a word:
- A printer of a different model, such as when the person chose P1S but owns a P1P.
- A printer already linked to another saved printer.
- A printer of the same model when the saved printer is linked to a different one.

The model is then told the search "has found no printer of this model", which is false for the last two.

## Medium: a known reason is dropped, but the model can recover

**4. `print_dialog_open`** looks up why the plate's last slice failed, then ignores it and says "Slice it with slice_start first" ([ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2106](../Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2106)). The model loses a step finding out again.

**5. `export_file`** says "Slice the plate first" even while a slice is running, and it also leaves out the failure reason ([OrcaOutputs.cpp:330](OrcaOutputs.cpp:330)).

**6. `slice_report`** answers `valid: false` during a slice with no mention that one is running ([ToolResults.cpp:795](../Agent/ToolResults.cpp:795)). That matters most when the person started the slice, because the model wasn't told.

**7. `printer_list`** leaves out a printer the search can hear when it is in cloud mode and the person isn't signed in ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2272](OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2272)). An empty list reads as "no printers". I didn't confirm whether saved Moonraker printers appear.

**8. The Add chat's "On the network now" line** can be wrong both ways ([printerInstructions.ts:189](../AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:189)). It is read once when the panel opens, and it can include a printer reached through the person's account that isn't on this network at all. It can also miss one that is on this network. When the list is empty, the line is left out, so the model can't tell "looked and found nothing" from "didn't look".

**9. Bambu plug-in install:** if the person closes the installer or the download fails, the model is told nothing ([PrinterConversation.cpp:253](../PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:253)).

## Low: an empty result gives no reason

**10. `presets_list`** skips hidden presets without counting them ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2326](OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2326)). A preset that is installed but hidden looks the same as one that doesn't exist.

**11. `settings_search`** returns an empty list when the setting exists but in another scope, such as searching printer settings for a process setting ([SettingsSupport.hpp:127](SettingsSupport.hpp:127)).

## Checked and fine
- **Reasons are passed on:** `project_open` and the import tools pass on the app's messages, and `slice_start` gives the refusal reason. Failed settings changes, mesh repair and G-code export also say why.
- **The app knows no more:** 3MF and STL export failures, "rendered nothing" and a failed calibration are generic because the app gets no reason itself. A calibration the person cancelled also looks like a failure, and the app can't tell the difference.

## Not fully covered
I read every refusal message in the tools, but not every successful result. I didn't check for empty sections in `object_analyze`, `slice_inspect` or `workspace_inspect`. I also didn't confirm whether settings hidden from editing show up in `settings_search`.
Double check your work. then Create a detailed report so that I can have another agent to confirm the list
